notes.Gilman Hall: Opened 1915. Georgian Revival after Homewood House. Clock tower rises 120 ft from the ground. Four floors; reads ~2.5 stories from Keyser because the lower floors sit into the slope. Faces Keyser Quad / Charles Street.
notes.Jenkins\u2013Mergenthaler Hall: Paired academic halls on the north side of Keyser Quad. OSM misspells Merganthaler; students say Jenkins or Mergenthaler.
notes.Maryland Hall: Whiting School. First occupied academic building on Homewood (1914). Three principal stories plus attic.
notes.Milton S. Eisenhower Library: Opened 1964. Reads as 1–2 stories from Keyser Quad; stacks continue underground. Connected to Brody.
notes.Brody Learning Commons: Library addition connected to MSE below grade. Reading rooms, cafe, special collections.
notes.Homewood Museum: Federal-style Homewood House (c. 1801). Palladian five-part plan, tetrastyle south portico, square cupola. Architectural model for the campus.
notes.Malone Hall: Whiting School. Georgian brick on Decker Quad; glass facade toward the BMA woods.
notes.Mason Hall: Visitor and admissions center on Decker Quadrangle (2008).
notes.Bloomberg Student Center: Opened 2025 on the former Mattin Center / Whitehead Hall site. Four stories.
notes.Keyser Quad: 2.44-acre academic lawn. Bounded by Gilman, Ames, Krieger, Jenkins–Mergenthaler, Remsen, and MSE Library.
notes.Wyman Quad: North–south academic quad south of Keyser, part of the original T-plan.
notes.Decker Quadrangle: West entrance quad: Mason, Malone, Hackerman, Garland.
notes.Freshman Quad: Residential lawn by the Alumni Memorial Residences.
notes.Homewood Field: Lacrosse / football. Schelle Pavilion on the west stand.
notes.Whitehead Hall: Demolished 2021 for the Bloomberg Student Center; not present.
